subject: Fast-path collaboration: S3-backed vector cold-tier connector (MinIO + Qdrant) / GTM sync
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: anna@min.io, marc@qdrant.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fast-path collaboration: S3-backed vector cold-tier connector (MinIO + Qdrant) / GTM sync

Hi Anna / Marc —

Quick note to propose a "fast-path" joint initiative between MinIO, Qdrant, and Redwood: we want to validate a lightweight S3-backed cold-tier connector that lets customers spill infrequently accessed vectors to S3 (MinIO-compatible) while keeping hot indexes in Qdrant. Objective is a 6-week PoC that proves correctness, recovery, and cost delta vs. fully hot-only deployments.

Why this matters: several customers are asking for predictable cost controls + simple on-prem S3 compatibility. Redwood can provide serving runtime hooks (batching + cache invalidation) and a launch partner GTM (co-marketing + joint demo).

Asks / proposed next steps:
- Quick architecture sync (30–45m) next week — can we get engineering representatives from both sides?
- Agree on PoC acceptance criteria: read/write correctness, failover behavior, rehydrate latency, and cost measurements.
- Draft SOW/roles: MinIO provides S3 endpoint + perf guidance, Qdrant implements the connector layer or adapter, Redwood provides serving integration and evaluation harness.
- Nominate legal/commercial contacts for a light revenue share / partner MSA template.

I'm looping in Vanessa for ops and Ben for commercial. If you're open, suggest Wed 5/20 9:30–10:15 PT or Thu 5/21 11:00–11:45 PT.

Jonas
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: rdw-minio-qdrant-fastpath-outline.pdf (overview, PoC acceptance criteria)

Subject: Re: Fast-path collaboration: S3-backed vector cold-tier connector (MinIO + Qdrant) / GTM sync

Thanks Jonas — this sounds very aligned with what a number of MinIO customers are asking for. Happy to jump in. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- MinIO can expose a standard S3-compatible endpoint and we can share a performance baseline for multi-part object vs single PUT semantics.
- We'll want to sanity-check the metadata format for vectors when evicted to S3 (index id, vector id, timestamp, small manifest).

I attached a short spec we typically use for S3 adapters. We can cover the manifest shape and expected consistency semantics during the sync. Proposed times work for me; I can do Wed 5/20 9:30 PT.

Anna Hall
Strategic Partnerships, MinIO
anna@min.io

Attachment: minio-connector-guidelines.pdf

Thanks all — great momentum. A few practical notes from Product/Programs: 

- PoC scope suggestion (6 weeks total):
  1) Week 0: architecture alignment + test plan sign-off (drivers: manifest schema, eviction policy, rehydrate API)
  2) Weeks 1–3: implementation + integration (Qdrant adapter + MinIO test bucket + Redwood runtime hooks)
  3) Week 4: validation (latency, correctness, fault injection)
  4) Week 5: customer demo + cost delta reporting
  5) Week 6: GTM materials + decision on broader pilot

- Acceptance criteria (examples):
  - Rehydrate P99 under 800ms for vectors < 8KB metadata
  - No silent data loss over 48h fault-injection windows
  - Measured token-cost delta <= 35% savings vs hot-only (by sample workload)

- Ops ask: we need a sample dataset and an isolated MinIO endpoint for perf tests. Can CloudBridge run the PoC infra for us? Ben — can you lead on a lightweight commercial note (rev share / credits / proof-of-work estimate)?

I can host the architecture sync Wed 5/20 9:30 PT — sending calendar invite.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships Programs | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Hi Vanessa / team —

CloudBridge can run the PoC infra and manage the validation runbooks. Quick estimate: 3–4 engineer-weeks and ~2 test VMs + a MinIO cluster (can run in our lab or on-prem) to reproduce latency/rehydration patterns. We typically deliver: test harness, scripted fault injections, and a hollow-customer demo.

Commercials: for a 6-week fixed-scope PoC we propose $24k fixed fee (covers infra ops, runbooks, and a short results report). We can open a credit against future pilot work if joint deals close.

Next steps from our side:
- Confirm PoC scope (Vanessa: can you confirm acceptance criteria above?)
- Share a sample dataset (we prefer ~50k vectors for a representative run)
- Provide an isolated MinIO endpoint + credentials (or we run in our lab)

Happy to talk through detail on the sync.

Sara Patel
Principal Architect, CloudBridge Consulting
sara@cloudbridge.com
